title: Sebastian and the Letter
premise: London, 1918. Quentin Fairweather, a woman passing as a male driver to survive, reads the letters she carries for the suffragist movement—until a child is abandoned at her door with a note ordering her to forget his face. The boy is the illegitimate son of a dying aristocrat whose family will erase him, and Quentin realizes the child's survival depends on a paper trail no one has yet thought to destroy. As the armistice euphoria sweeps the country and official histories are written by the winners, Quentin races to smuggle testimony, letters, and her own dangerous confession into the record. She ends by choosing visibility over safety: she signs her real name to the deposition, loses her disguise and her quiet life, but gains a son and a found family willing to stand beside her.
about_author: Mara Quintana is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suffragist correspondence before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about the people official records forgot.

chapters.title: The Man Behind the Wheel
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. We meet Quentin in her carefully constructed life as a male chauffeur for suffragist organizer Mrs. Aldous, reading letters by lamplight and filing away secrets. Emotional beat: the comfort and loneliness of invisibility, and the first crack in it when she lingers over one letter too long.

chapters.title: Instructions to Forget
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A stormy night delivery ends with a toddler left in her care and a note: 'Forget the face.' The handwriting belongs to someone Quentin recognizes from intercepted letters. Emotional beat: fear and reluctant tenderness as she realizes the child is evidence someone wants erased.

chapters.title: What the Letters Knew
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, with a flashback to her own escape from her family years earlier. She cross-references old letters and pieces together the boy's parentage—a dying lord, a silenced maid, a ruthless heir. Emotional beat: recognition; Quentin sees her own survival story mirrored in the child's.

chapters.title: Mrs. Aldous's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dual pressure chapter, Quentin's POV. Mrs. Aldous discovers the boy and offers help—at the price of Quentin taking on a risky courier run through police checkpoints during armistice week. Emotional beat: the suffragist's pragmatism versus Quentin's terror of exposure.

chapters.title: The Heir's Men
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The lord's family sends investigators; a near-discovery at a boarding house forces Quentin to move the boy in the night. A kind neighbor, Ada, helps without asking questions. Emotional beat: the found family begins forming, but so does the hunt.

chapters.title: Victors' Ink
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, interleaved with excerpts of official histories being drafted. She learns the heir is funding a sanitized memoir and that witnesses are being paid off or silenced. Emotional beat: outrage crystallizing into resolve—she must get the truth on the record first.

chapters.title: The Dying Lord's Confession
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Risking everything, she arranges a bedside meeting; the dying lord dictates a letter acknowledging the boy and entrusts her with documents. Emotional beat: grief and fragile hope, undercut by the knowledge that paper can be stolen as easily as kept.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Except the Truth
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The heir's men ransack her lodgings and burn what they find; the boy goes missing in the chaos. Ada and Mrs. Aldous mobilize the movement's network to search. Emotional beat: despair at rock bottom, then the discovery that Quentin had already hidden copies—her archiving habit saves them.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, climax. In a crowded public inquiry into war orphans, Quentin sheds her disguise, gives her real name, and enters the lord's confession, the letters, and her testimony into evidence before the heir's lawyers can stop her. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into triumph; visibility chosen at last.

chapters.title: Sebastian
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, epilogue one year later. The boy—now legally Sebastian Fairweather—plays in the garden of the small house Quentin shares with Ada and Mrs. Aldous. Quentin writes the final letter herself, addressed to the historians of the future. Emotional beat: peace earned, family found, survival redefined as living openly.
